# basal benchmark records

Local A/B benchmark records for optimisation work on [basal](https://github.com/rkinas/basal), measured on one
specific machine. Each record compares **two commits** — normally the newest `upstream/main` of the original
repository against a commit from the fork `bajor/basal` — and states whether the candidate is better, worse,
unchanged or broken, with every metric the basal CLIs produce and the raw output behind it.

This repository holds records and the harness that makes them. It never modifies basal.

## The machine every record describes

| | |
|---|---|
| Model | MacBook Air `Mac16,12` |
| Chip | Apple M4, 10 cores (4 performance + 6 efficiency) |
| Memory | 16 GB unified |
| macOS | 26.5.2 (Darwin 25.5.0), arm64 |
| Benchmark interpreter | `~/basal-env/bin/python`, CPython 3.12.13 arm64 |
| Stack | torch 2.15.0 (MPS), transformers 5.17.0, mlx 0.32.4, llama-cpp-python 0.3.37 |
| Weights | `$HF_HOME` = `/Volumes/Vimap H3 t7/ai/cache/huggingface` (external drive) |

**This is a fanless laptop.** Its run-to-run drift is routinely larger than the optimisations being measured, which
is why every record carries a measured noise floor and why no change smaller than that floor is ever called an
improvement. Records measured here are comparable with each other and with nothing else.

Two consequences are baked into `harness/config.py` rather than left as options:

- **fp32 reference only for `mini`.** The 4.5B model needs about 18 GB in fp32. Only the 1.5B model keeps a true
  fp32 correctness reference; the 4.5B unit's reference is bf16 `mps`.
- **Benchmarks need real GPU access.** A sandboxed shell cannot reach Metal, so the harness must run outside it.

## Run one

```bash
~/basal-env/bin/python harness/run_record.py --candidate <your-commit>     # baseline: upstream/main
~/basal-env/bin/python harness/run_record.py --candidate HEAD --profile quick --no-commit
```

| profile | covers | repeats | roughly |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quick` | mini, `mps` + `mlx` | 1 | 20 min |
| `standard` | mini + 4.5B, all modes | 3 | 1–2 h |
| `thorough` (default) | all four units, all modes | 5 interleaved | 4–6 h |

Agents: read `.claude/skills/basal-benchmark/SKILL.md` first. It carries the operational constraints that silently
invalidate a run.

## How to read a record

`records/<UTC timestamp>__<baseline>__<candidate>/`

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `record.md` | the verdict, then every number that produced it. Start here. |
| `record.json` | the same content as data |
| `meta.json` | both commits, the environment, phase timings, dependency drift, interleave order |
| `answers_diff.json` | the cross-commit answer comparison, per mode and per question |
| `raw/` | every command's own `--out` JSON and full log, unmodified |

`INDEX.md` lists every record, newest first.

### The verdicts

| verdict | meaning |
|---|---|
| `BROKEN` | a blocking correctness gate failed. Speed is not the question. |
| `REGRESSION` | measurably slower, nothing broken |
| `MIXED` | some measurements improved and others regressed, both beyond the noise floor |
| `ANSWERS CHANGED` | the engine decides differently, with no measurable speed difference |
| `TIMING NOT ASSESSED` | correctness checked, but too few repeats to separate a difference from drift |
| `NO CHANGE` | nothing moved further than this machine's own drift |
| `IMPROVEMENT` | measurably faster, and decides the same |
| `IMPROVEMENT WITH CHANGED ANSWERS` | faster, but the answers moved. The win is not free. |

A speed claim is only as good as the noise floor beside it. `record.md` prints the noise floor and the threshold for
every metric, so any claim can be checked against the scatter that produced it.

**A profile with one repeat per side gives no speed verdict at all.** Measured here: two commits differing only by a
version string reported 25-42% "regressions" at one repeat, because the second side ran on a warmer machine. At n=1
a side's noise floor is 0.0 by construction, so drift is indistinguishable from a result. Those metrics are printed
with `not judged` and the reason beside them, and the record's headline says timing was not assessed.

### What is measured

Offline latency and throughput (`basal-bench`), option-order sensitivity (`--order-check`), backend agreement with
bootstrap intervals and question independence (`basal-agree`), HTTP latency and throughput (`basal-loadtest`),
server determinism under load, the full test suite, and — the one thing basal cannot report by itself — a
**cross-commit answer diff**: the same items served by both commits with `--deterministic`, one request at a time,
with every probability compared.

`basal-bench`'s own `agree` column compares *modes within one run*. It cannot tell you whether your commit changed
what the engine decides. That is what `harness/compare_answers.py` is for.

## The harness

| file | responsibility |
|---|---|
| `config.py` | units, profiles, thresholds, metric directions — edit this rather than passing flags |
| `preflight.py` | machine facts, and the gates a measured record must pass |
| `phases.py` | the command lines, as pure data |
| `execute.py` | worktrees, subprocesses, the served-server lifecycle, weight resolution |
| `metrics.py` | each tool's JSON into one comparable shape |
| `verdict.py` | noise floor, per-metric classification, gates, overall verdict |
| `compare_answers.py` | the cross-commit answer diff (also a standalone CLI) |
| `report.py` | rendering `record.md` |
| `run_record.py` | the orchestrator |

Its own tests cover the logic whose failure would produce confident false claims:

```bash
cd harness && ~/basal-env/bin/python -m pytest -q
```

### Calibrate before trusting a comparison

```bash
~/basal-env/bin/python harness/run_record.py --candidate HEAD --baseline HEAD \
  --allow-same-commit --profile quick --no-commit
```

The same commit against itself must report `NO CHANGE` everywhere. The noise floor it prints is this machine's real
measurement precision. If it reports any `better` or `WORSE`, the thresholds are too tight for current conditions
and no comparison should be believed until that is fixed.

## Setting the machine up again

```bash
uv python install cpython-3.12-macos-aarch64-none
uv venv --python cpython-3.12-macos-aarch64-none ~/basal-env
uv pip install --python ~/basal-env/bin/python "<path-to-basal>[test,mlx]"   # NOT -e
uv pip install --python ~/basal-env/bin/python "llama-cpp-python>=0.3.36"    # --mode gguf, compiles with Metal
git -C <path-to-basal> remote add upstream https://github.com/rkinas/basal.git
```

The install is **non-editable** deliberately. The harness benchmarks each commit from its own `git worktree` and
relies on `python -m` putting the worktree first on `sys.path`. An editable install registers a meta-path finder
that wins over `sys.path`, which would silently benchmark the wrong code. `harness/execute.py:check_shadowing`
verifies this per run and aborts if it is ever untrue.

"""Tests for rendering a record. A record that cannot be rendered is a run thrown away, so this covers the
partial-data cases a real run produces: a mode that failed, a backend with no memory reading, a skipped phase.

  cd harness && python -m pytest test_report.py -q
"""
import pytest

from report import index_line, render
from verdict import Gate, assess, compare_series

META = {
    "record_id": "2026-11-19T0930Z__50ce799__abc1234",
    "profile": "quick", "repeats": 1,
    "baseline": {"sha": "50ce7997520b336e214d6f916aa3e0e4ed83cdc7", "short": "50ce799",
                 "subject": "chore(release): basal 2.8.1", "date": "2026-11-15T10:00:00+01:00"},
    "candidate": {"sha": "abc1234567890abc1234567890abc1234567890a", "short": "abc1234",
                  "subject": "perf(engine): fuse the readout gather", "date": "2026-11-19T09:00:00+01:00"},
    "questions": "questions/bench_items.jsonl", "question_count": 44,
    "interleave": "B/C", "started_at": "2026-11-19T09:30:00+00:00",
    "finished_at": "2026-11-19T09:40:00+00:00", "wall_clock_s": 600.0,
    "environment": {"hardware": {"model": "Mac16,12", "chip": "Apple M4", "memory": "16 GB",
                                 "cores": "proc 10:4:6:0", "macos": "26.5.2", "arch": "arm64"},
                    "power": {"source": "AC"},
                    "stack": {"python": "3.12.13", "torch": "2.15.0", "mps": True,
                              "transformers": "5.17.0", "mlx": "0.32.4", "llama_cpp": "0.3.37"},
                    "hf_home": {"path": "/Volumes/drive/hf"}},
    "phases": [{"name": "bench mini-bf16 baseline rep0", "seconds": 61.2, "status": "ok"}],
}

SERIES = {("mini-bf16", "mps", "lat2_ms"): {"baseline": [141.2, 139.0], "candidate": [120.0, 118.0]},
          ("mini-bf16", "mps", "dec_s"): {"baseline": [7.0, 7.1], "candidate": [8.2, 8.3]}}

ANSWER_DIFF = [{"unit": "mini-bf16", "mode": "mps", "verdict": "IDENTICAL",
                "overall": {"compared": 120, "identical": 120, "flips": 0, "near_tie_flips": 0,
                            "max_abs_dp": 0.0, "p99_abs_dp": 0.0}}]

AGREE = [{"unit": "mini-bf16", "side": "baseline", "backend": "mps", "reference": "eager-fp32",
          "readouts_agreement": 1.0, "near_ties": 0, "mean_dp": 1e-6, "max_dp": 2e-5,
          "decision_agreement": 1.0, "independence": 1.0, "accuracy": 0.705, "gate_passed": True}]

ORDERS = [{"unit": "mini-bf16", "mode": "mps", "side": "baseline", "flip_reversed": 0.09,
           "flip_rotated": 0.09, "flip_any": 0.11, "first_share": 0.34, "acc_given": 0.70,
           "acc_reversed": 0.68, "acc_rotated": 0.70, "acc_mean2": 0.71, "agree_mean2": 0.98,
           "lat_mean2_ms": 141.0}]


def jsonable(series):
    return {f"{u}|{m}|{k}": v for (u, m, k), v in series.items()}


@pytest.fixture
def rendered():
    comparisons = compare_series(SERIES)
    assessment = assess(comparisons, [Gate("tests", True, "no new failures")], answers_changed=False)
    return render(META, assessment, ANSWER_DIFF, AGREE, ORDERS, jsonable(SERIES))


def test_given_a_faster_candidate_when_rendered_then_the_verdict_leads(rendered):
    assert rendered.startswith("# IMPROVEMENT: `50ce799` → `abc1234`")


def test_given_a_record_when_rendered_then_both_full_shas_appear(rendered):
    """A record that does not name its exact commits cannot be reproduced."""
    assert META["baseline"]["sha"] in rendered
    assert META["candidate"]["sha"] in rendered


def test_given_a_record_when_rendered_then_every_speed_claim_carries_its_threshold(rendered):
    """A change without the bar it had to clear is not a claim a reader can check."""
    assert "noise floor" in rendered and "threshold" in rendered
    assert "`lat2_ms`" in rendered and "`dec_s`" in rendered


def test_given_a_record_when_rendered_then_the_machine_and_power_state_are_stated(rendered):
    assert "Apple M4" in rendered and "16 GB" in rendered
    assert "**Power during the run**: AC" in rendered


def test_given_a_broken_candidate_when_rendered_then_the_reason_is_explained():
    assessment = assess(compare_series(SERIES),
                        [Gate("tests", False, "1 test fails only on the candidate: tests/test_engine.py::test_x")],
                        answers_changed=False)
    out = render(META, assessment, ANSWER_DIFF, AGREE, ORDERS, jsonable(SERIES))
    assert out.startswith("# BROKEN:")
    assert "## Why it is broken" in out
    assert "tests/test_engine.py::test_x" in out


def test_given_dependency_drift_when_rendered_then_it_is_called_out():
    """Two commits with different pins did not run on one environment; the record must not hide that."""
    meta = {**META, "dependency_drift": ['-  "torch>=2.11",', '+  "torch>=2.16",']}
    assessment = assess(compare_series(SERIES), [], answers_changed=False)
    out = render(meta, assessment, ANSWER_DIFF, AGREE, ORDERS, jsonable(SERIES))
    assert "Dependency drift between the two commits" in out
    assert "torch>=2.16" in out


def test_given_skipped_phases_when_rendered_then_it_says_so_rather_than_showing_empty_tables():
    assessment = assess(compare_series(SERIES), [], answers_changed=False)
    out = render(META, assessment, [], [], [], jsonable(SERIES))
    assert "The answer diff did not run in this profile." in out
    assert "`basal-agree` did not run in this profile." in out
    assert "`basal-bench --order-check` did not run in this profile." in out


def test_given_a_metric_measured_on_one_side_only_when_rendered_then_it_shows_as_not_judged():
    """A mode that failed on one side must read as not judged, never as unchanged."""
    series = {("mini-bf16", "gguf", "lat2_ms"): {"baseline": [133.1], "candidate": []}}
    assessment = assess(compare_series(series), [], answers_changed=False)
    out = render(META, assessment, ANSWER_DIFF, AGREE, ORDERS, jsonable(series))
    assert "not judged" in out
    assert "the metric is missing on one side" in out


def test_given_too_few_repeats_when_rendered_then_the_table_says_why_no_verdict_was_given():
    """The numbers are shown; the reason the harness declined to judge them is shown beside them."""
    series = {("mini-bf16", "mps", "lat2_ms"): {"baseline": [254.8], "candidate": [362.5]}}
    assessment = assess(compare_series(series), [Gate("tests", True, "ok")], answers_changed=False)
    out = render(META, assessment, ANSWER_DIFF, AGREE, ORDERS, jsonable(series))
    assert out.startswith("# TIMING NOT ASSESSED:")
    assert "not judged" in out
    assert "drift cannot be separated" in out
    assert "254.8" in out and "362.5" in out        # still reported, so the run is not wasted


def test_given_a_null_memory_reading_when_rendered_then_the_row_is_still_readable():
    series = {("mini-bf16", "gguf", "mem_gb"): {"baseline": [], "candidate": []}}
    assessment = assess([], [], answers_changed=False)
    out = render(META, assessment, ANSWER_DIFF, AGREE, ORDERS, jsonable(series))
    assert "`mem_gb`" in out


def test_given_changed_answers_with_a_speed_win_when_rendered_then_the_win_is_qualified():
    assessment = assess(compare_series(SERIES), [Gate("answers", False, "CHANGED", blocking=False)],
                        answers_changed=True)
    out = render(META, assessment, ANSWER_DIFF, AGREE, ORDERS, jsonable(SERIES))
    assert out.startswith("# IMPROVEMENT WITH CHANGED ANSWERS:")
    assert "not free" in out


def test_given_every_possible_verdict_then_a_headline_exists_for_it():
    """A missing headline would raise KeyError while writing the record, losing a finished run's results."""
    from report import HEADLINE
    from verdict import Overall
    assert set(HEADLINE) == set(Overall), set(Overall) - set(HEADLINE)


def test_given_every_possible_verdict_when_rendered_then_it_does_not_raise():
    from verdict import Assessment, Overall
    for overall in Overall:
        assessment = Assessment(overall=overall, speed=Overall.NO_CHANGE,
                                gates=[Gate("tests", True, "ok")], comparisons=compare_series(SERIES))
        out = render(META, assessment, ANSWER_DIFF, AGREE, ORDERS, jsonable(SERIES))
        assert out.startswith(f"# {overall.value}:")

Running. While it goes, let me be clear about what battery operation does and doesn't invalidate, since it affects how you should read what comes back.

**It does not invalidate the dry run's purpose.** That run tests whether the harness mechanics work and whether the verdict logic reaches the right conclusion on a pair of commits that are computationally identical. Both sides are measured under the same conditions within the same run, with alternating order — so a correct `NO CHANGE` is still a correct result.

**It does change what calibration means.** The noise floor measured on battery is the floor *for benchmarking on battery*. That's arguably the more useful number if battery is how you'll actually work — but it won't transfer to AC records, and mixing the two in one `INDEX.md` would be comparing different machines. The new warning block in `record.md` is there to stop that confusion.

**One risk I'll watch:** macOS throttles harder as the battery drains, and Low Power Mode may engage automatically at 20%. If the battery falls far during a run, drift grows — which the noise floor will capture rather than hide.

Summary of this turn's work while the benchmark runs:

**Proceeding on battery as you asked.** I've stopped raising it — it's your call, and I've made the harness record the consequence rather than argue about it.

**Two integrity fixes went in, both prompted by actually doing it on battery:**

1. A record measured with `--skip-preflight-gates` now **says so at the top of `record.md`**, listing the unmet conditions. Previously that fact lived only in `meta.json`, so someone reading the verdict would have seen an ordinary record.

2. The harness now **samples power at start and end** and warns if it changed. This came from noticing your two `pmset` readings disagreed. Worth repeating as a hardware observation: `AC attached; not charging` followed seconds later by `discharging` suggests a **flaky adapter, cable, or port** — not a deliberate unplugging. If you *did* intend it plugged in, that's a hardware fault worth checking, independent of benchmarking.

The reason this distinction matters technically: interleaving the two sides cancels *gradual* drift, which is why the design works on a thermally noisy machine. It cannot cancel a *step change* halfway through, where one commit is measured on wall power and the other isn't. That case needed detecting rather than averaging.

When the run completes I'll report the verdict against the known-correct answer (`NO CHANGE`, identical answers), then run the calibration — which on battery will tell you the noise floor for benchmarking the way you're actually working.

def noise_floor(values: list[float]) -> float:
    """Spread of one side's repeats, relative to its own median. One repeat has no measurable spread, hence 0.0.

    Descriptive only. It is reported so a reader can see the scatter, but it does not decide anything: the range of a
    handful of observations underestimates true variability and is itself highly variable, which is precisely how an
    earlier version of this file turned a 9.6% drift into an "improvement". The decision is made by permutation_p.
    """
    usable = [v for v in values if v is not None]
    if len(usable) < 2:
        return 0.0
    median = statistics.median(usable)
    if median == 0:
        return 0.0
    return (max(usable) - min(usable)) / abs(median)


def _median_gap(left: list[float], right: list[float]) -> float:
    return abs(statistics.median(right) - statistics.median(left))


def permutation_p(baseline: list[float], candidate: list[float]) -> float:
    """Exact two-sided permutation test on the difference of medians: P(a split this separated | no real difference).

    Under the null the two labels are interchangeable, so every way of dealing the pooled measurements into two
    groups of the original sizes is equally likely. The p-value is the share of those splits whose median gap is at
    least the observed one.

    Exchangeability is what interleaving the two sides buys. Were one commit measured entirely before the other,
    thermal drift would make the labels *not* interchangeable and this test would be measuring warm-up.

    Returns 1.0 when either side is empty, so a missing side can never look significant.
    """
    if not baseline or not candidate:
        return 1.0
    pooled = baseline + candidate
    n, total_n = len(baseline), len(pooled)
    observed = _median_gap(baseline, candidate)

"""Tests for the verdict rules. A fault here would state improvements that never happened — which this harness has
already done twice, so the cases below include the real measurements that fooled it.

  cd harness && python -m pytest test_verdict.py -q
"""
import math

from config import Direction
from verdict import (ALPHA, MIN_REPEATS_TO_JUDGE, Gate, MetricVerdict, Overall, accuracy_gate, assess, classify,
                     compare_series, memory_gate, noise_floor, permutation_p, speed_verdict, tests_gate)


def latency(values):
    return classify(values["baseline"], values["candidate"], Direction.LOWER_BETTER)


# --- the exact permutation test ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_given_n_per_side_then_the_best_attainable_p_value_is_two_over_the_arrangements():
    """The floor on significance: with n per side there are C(2n, n) splits, and two of them are as extreme as
    perfect separation (one per label ordering)."""
    for n in (2, 3, 4, 5):
        separated = permutation_p([1.0 * i for i in range(n)], [100.0 + i for i in range(n)])
        assert separated == 2 / math.comb(2 * n, n), n


def test_given_the_minimum_repeats_then_alpha_is_attainable_and_one_fewer_cannot_reach_it():
    """This is why MIN_REPEATS_TO_JUDGE is what it is, rather than a number someone liked."""
    n = MIN_REPEATS_TO_JUDGE
    assert 2 / math.comb(2 * n, n) <= ALPHA
    assert 2 / math.comb(2 * (n - 1), n - 1) > ALPHA


def test_given_identical_measurements_when_tested_then_p_is_one():
    assert permutation_p([10.0] * 4, [10.0] * 4) == 1.0


def test_given_an_empty_side_when_tested_then_p_is_one_so_it_cannot_look_significant():
    assert permutation_p([], [1.0, 2.0]) == 1.0
    assert permutation_p([1.0, 2.0], []) == 1.0


def test_given_fully_overlapping_spreads_when_tested_then_p_is_far_above_alpha():
    base = [100.0, 110.0, 120.0, 130.0]
    cand = [105.0, 115.0, 125.0, 135.0]
    assert permutation_p(base, cand) > ALPHA


def test_given_the_same_measurements_twice_when_tested_then_the_p_value_is_identical():
    """A record must be reproducible from its raw files; a sampled test uses a fixed seed for that reason."""
    base, cand = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], [9.0, 10.0, 11.0, 12.0]
    assert permutation_p(base, cand) == permutation_p(base, cand)


# --- what the two false verdicts looked like -------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_given_the_measurements_that_produced_a_false_regression_then_no_verdict_is_given():
    """Real data, 2026-11-19 dry run at one repeat: 4e81a35 vs 50ce799 differ only in __version__ and a date, and
    the harness called this a 42% regression because the candidate ran second on a warmer machine."""
    result = latency({"baseline": [254.8], "candidate": [362.5]})
    assert result["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.UNKNOWN
    assert "no verdict is possible" in result["why_unknown"]


def test_given_the_measurements_that_produced_a_false_improvement_then_no_verdict_is_given():
    """Real data, same pair at two repeats, mlx lat2_ms. The candidate's two samples happened to land close
    together, collapsing the range-based noise floor to 2.9% and letting a 9.6% drift read as an improvement."""
    result = latency({"baseline": [313.9, 344.5], "candidate": [293.4, 302.0]})
    assert result["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.UNKNOWN
    assert "2 repeat(s) per side" in result["why_unknown"]


def test_given_that_same_scatter_at_four_repeats_then_it_is_still_not_called_a_difference():
    """Even with enough repeats to permit a verdict, that much overlap does not support one."""
    result = latency({"baseline": [313.9, 344.5, 320.1, 338.0], "candidate": [293.4, 302.0, 341.7, 318.9]})
    assert result["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.SAME
    assert result["p_value"] > ALPHA


# --- classification -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_given_a_clean_separated_latency_drop_when_classified_then_better():
    result = latency({"baseline": [100.0, 101.0, 99.0, 100.5], "candidate": [80.0, 81.0, 79.0, 80.5]})
    assert result["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.BETTER
    assert result["p_value"] <= ALPHA
    assert result["improvement"] > 0


def test_given_a_clean_separated_latency_rise_when_classified_then_worse():
    result = latency({"baseline": [80.0, 81.0, 79.0, 80.5], "candidate": [100.0, 101.0, 99.0, 100.5]})
    assert result["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.WORSE
    assert result["improvement"] < 0


def test_given_a_reproducible_but_tiny_difference_when_classified_then_same():
    """Statistically solid, operationally irrelevant: the practical threshold has to be met as well."""
    result = latency({"baseline": [100.0, 100.1, 100.0, 100.1], "candidate": [99.0, 99.1, 99.0, 99.1]})
    assert result["p_value"] <= ALPHA           # perfectly separated
    assert abs(result["improvement"]) < 0.03    # but only ~1%
    assert result["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.SAME


def test_given_a_large_but_erratic_difference_when_classified_then_same():
    """The mirror image: big median gap, spreads that overlap, so nothing is established."""
    result = latency({"baseline": [60.0, 140.0, 80.0, 120.0], "candidate": [55.0, 135.0, 70.0, 100.0]})
    assert abs(result["improvement"]) > 0.03
    assert result["p_value"] > ALPHA
    assert result["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.SAME


def test_given_too_few_repeats_when_classified_then_the_reason_names_the_attainable_p_value():
    result = latency({"baseline": [100.0, 101.0, 99.0], "candidate": [80.0, 81.0, 79.0]})
    assert result["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.UNKNOWN
    assert "0.10" in result["why_unknown"]
    assert result["improvement"] > 0            # still reported, so the run is not wasted


def test_given_one_repeat_on_one_side_only_when_classified_then_the_weaker_side_governs():
    result = latency({"baseline": [100.0, 101.0, 99.0, 100.5, 100.2], "candidate": [80.0]})
    assert result["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.UNKNOWN


def test_given_higher_is_better_when_throughput_rises_then_better():
    result = classify([10.0, 10.1, 9.9, 10.0], [20.0, 20.1, 19.9, 20.0], Direction.HIGHER_BETTER)
    assert result["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.BETTER


def test_given_higher_is_better_when_throughput_falls_then_worse():
    result = classify([20.0, 20.1, 19.9, 20.0], [10.0, 10.1, 9.9, 10.0], Direction.HIGHER_BETTER)
    assert result["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.WORSE


def test_given_a_missing_side_when_classified_then_unknown_not_same():
    """A mode that failed to run must never be reported as unchanged."""
    assert classify([], [100.0], Direction.LOWER_BETTER)["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.UNKNOWN


def test_given_a_zero_baseline_when_classified_then_unknown():
    assert classify([0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [5.0] * 4, Direction.LOWER_BETTER)["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.UNKNOWN


# --- the noise floor, now descriptive only --------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_given_one_repeat_when_noise_floor_computed_then_it_is_zero():
    assert noise_floor([100.0]) == 0.0


def test_given_repeats_when_noise_floor_computed_then_it_is_the_spread_over_the_median():
    assert noise_floor([90.0, 100.0, 110.0]) == 0.2


def test_given_a_tiny_observed_spread_when_classified_then_it_no_longer_licenses_a_verdict():
    """The old rule let a small range alone justify a claim. It cannot any more: p decides."""
    result = latency({"baseline": [100.0, 100.0], "candidate": [97.0, 97.0]})
    assert noise_floor(result and [100.0, 100.0]) == 0.0
    assert result["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.UNKNOWN


# --- aggregation ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def series(metric, baseline, candidate, unit="mini-bf16", mode="mps"):
    return {(unit, mode, metric): {"baseline": baseline, "candidate": candidate}}


FAST = [80.0, 81.0, 79.0, 80.5]
SLOW = [100.0, 101.0, 99.0, 100.5]
HIGH_RATE = [20.0, 20.1, 19.9, 20.0]
LOW_RATE = [10.0, 10.1, 9.9, 10.0]


def test_given_a_non_timing_metric_when_series_compared_then_it_is_skipped():
    """Accuracy and memory go through gates, not the significance path."""
    assert compare_series(series("acc", [0.9] * 4, [0.9] * 4)) == []


def test_given_mixed_primary_metrics_when_speed_judged_then_mixed():
    comparisons = compare_series({**series("lat2_ms", SLOW, FAST),
                                  **series("dec_s", HIGH_RATE, LOW_RATE)})
    assert speed_verdict(comparisons) is Overall.MIXED


def test_given_only_secondary_metrics_moved_when_speed_judged_then_the_primaries_still_decide():
    """load_s moved hugely, but it is not a primary metric, so on its own it decides nothing."""
    comparisons = compare_series({**series("load_s", SLOW, FAST),
                                  **series("lat2_ms", SLOW, SLOW)})
    assert speed_verdict(comparisons) is Overall.NO_CHANGE


def test_given_no_primary_metric_was_measured_when_speed_judged_then_it_is_not_assessed():
    comparisons = compare_series(series("load_s", SLOW, FAST))
    assert speed_verdict(comparisons) is Overall.TIMING_NOT_ASSESSED


def test_given_no_primary_metric_could_be_judged_when_speed_judged_then_it_is_not_assessed():
    comparisons = compare_series(series("lat2_ms", [254.8], [362.5]))
    assert speed_verdict(comparisons) is Overall.TIMING_NOT_ASSESSED


# --- gates ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_given_memory_growth_beyond_tolerance_when_gated_then_it_fails():
    gate = memory_gate(series("mem_gb", [4.0] * 4, [5.0] * 4))
    assert not gate.passed and gate.blocking


def test_given_memory_growth_within_tolerance_when_gated_then_it_passes():
    assert memory_gate(series("mem_gb", [4.0] * 4, [4.2] * 4)).passed


def test_given_no_memory_measurements_when_gated_then_it_is_non_blocking():
    """GGUF and CPU backends report no memory; that is a gap in the data, not a failure."""
    gate = memory_gate({})
    assert gate.passed and not gate.blocking


def test_given_an_accuracy_drop_beyond_the_baseline_spread_when_gated_then_it_fails():
    gate = accuracy_gate(series("acc", [0.900] * 4, [0.850] * 4))
    assert not gate.passed


def test_given_an_accuracy_drop_within_the_baseline_spread_when_gated_then_it_passes():
    """The baseline itself wandered by 0.05 between repeats, so a 0.02 drop says nothing."""
    assert accuracy_gate(series("acc", [0.88, 0.90, 0.93, 0.91], [0.88] * 4)).passed


def test_given_a_test_failing_only_on_the_candidate_when_gated_then_it_fails():
    gate = tests_gate({"failed_tests": []}, {"failed_tests": ["tests/test_engine.py::test_x"]})
    assert not gate.passed


def test_given_a_test_failing_on_both_sides_when_gated_then_it_passes_as_pre_existing():

Found it — and it's a real power problem, not just a wrong test.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The median is **insensitive to the tails**: with n=4, swapping the innermost values (81 ↔ 99) leaves both group medians unchanged, so 4 arrangements tie at the observed gap instead of 2. At n=5 this gets worse — perfect separation gives p = 12/252 = **0.0476**, barely under 0.05. A genuinely clean 20% improvement would sit right on the significance boundary.

The standard fix is the **rank-sum (Mann-Whitney) statistic**: as outlier-robust as the median, but it uses every observation's rank, so perfect separation gives exactly 2 extreme arrangements — p = 2/252 = 0.0079 at n=5. The median stays as the *descriptive* summary; the rank sum does the *deciding*.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

def _median_gap(left: list[float], right: list[float]) -> float:
    return abs(statistics.median(right) - statistics.median(left))


def permutation_p(baseline: list[float], candidate: list[float]) -> float:
    """Exact two-sided permutation test on the difference of medians: P(a split this separated | no real difference).

    Under the null the two labels are interchangeable, so every way of dealing the pooled measurements into two
    groups of the original sizes is equally likely. The p-value is the share of those splits whose median gap is at
    least the observed one.

    Exchangeability is what interleaving the two sides buys. Were one commit measured entirely before the other,
    thermal drift would make the labels *not* interchangeable and this test would be measuring warm-up.

    Returns 1.0 when either side is empty, so a missing side can never look significant.
    """
    if not baseline or not candidate:
        return 1.0
    pooled = baseline + candidate
    n, total_n = len(baseline), len(pooled)
    observed = _median_gap(baseline, candidate)
    arrangements = math.comb(total_n, n)
    tolerance = 1e-12

    def split(indices: tuple[int, ...] | list[int]) -> float:
        chosen = set(indices)
        left = [pooled[i] for i in chosen]
        right = [pooled[i] for i in range(total_n) if i not in chosen]
        return _median_gap(left, right)

    if arrangements <= MAX_EXACT_ARRANGEMENTS:
        extreme = sum(1 for idx in itertools.combinations(range(total_n), n)
                      if split(idx) >= observed - tolerance)
        return extreme / arrangements
    rng = random.Random(0)  # fixed seed: the same measurements always give the same p-value
    indices = list(range(total_n))
    extreme = 0
    for _ in range(PERMUTATION_SAMPLES):
        rng.shuffle(indices)
        if split(indices[:n]) >= observed - tolerance:
            extreme += 1
    return extreme / PERMUTATION_SAMPLES

    """Ranks from 1, with tied values sharing their average rank (the standard tie correction)."""
    order = sorted(range(len(values)), key=values.__getitem__)

Found it — and it's a real power problem, not just a wrong test.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The median is **insensitive to the tails**: with n=4, swapping the innermost values (81 ↔ 99) leaves both group medians unchanged, so 4 arrangements tie at the observed gap instead of 2. At n=5 this gets worse — perfect separation gives p = 12/252 = **0.0476**, barely under 0.05. A genuinely clean 20% improvement would sit right on the significance boundary.

The standard fix is the **rank-sum (Mann-Whitney) statistic**: as outlier-robust as the median, but it uses every observation's rank, so perfect separation gives exactly 2 extreme arrangements — p = 2/252 = 0.0079 at n=5. The median stays as the *descriptive* summary; the rank sum does the *deciding*.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

fix(verdict): decide with an exact rank-sum permutation test, not a range heuristic

The harness produced a false verdict on both dry runs of 4e81a35 vs 50ce799 -
commits differing only in __version__ and a RELEASE_DATE string, so "no change"
was known to be correct. One repeat per side gave "42% regression"; two gave
"9.6% improvement". The served answers were byte-identical in both runs, so only
the timing rule was at fault.

Why the heuristic was unsound. It compared a difference of medians against
max(observed range / median, 3%). The range of a handful of observations
underestimates true variability and is itself highly variable: in the second run
the candidate's two samples landed 2.9% apart while the baseline's spanned 9.3%,
so the threshold collapsed and a 9.6% drift cleared it by 0.3 points. A range is
not a test; it carries no notion of how likely a separation is by chance.

The decision is now an exact two-sided permutation test over the repeats, and
BETTER/WORSE requires both p <= 0.05 (unlikely to be chance) and improvement
beyond 3% (large enough to matter). Either condition alone is useless: a tiny
reproducible difference is real and irrelevant, an erratic large one the reverse.

The statistic is the rank sum (Mann-Whitney), not the median difference, even
though medians are what the record reports. A median ignores the tails, so with
four values per side swapping the two innermost observations leaves both medians
unchanged; arrangements tie at the observed gap and the p-value inflates. At five
repeats even perfect separation only reached p = 0.048, which would have put
every genuine clean win on the significance boundary. Ranks use every observation
while staying as outlier-robust as a median, giving exactly 2/C(2n, n) for
perfect separation: 0.029 at n=4, 0.0079 at n=5.

MIN_REPEATS_TO_JUDGE is now 4, and derived rather than chosen: with n per side
the smallest attainable p-value is 2/C(2n, n), which is 0.33 at n=2 and 0.10 at
n=3. Below four, significance is unreachable whatever the data says. The standard
profile moves from 3 to 4 repeats for the same reason - at 3 it could never have
concluded anything about timing - and its bench_lat_n drops 50 to 30 to pay for
the extra repeat.

Both false-verdict datasets are now regression tests, and scatter is documented
as descriptive only.

The decisive validation is running. Here's what happened this turn, which is the most important finding of the whole session.

## My verdict logic was unsound, and the dry runs proved it twice

Both runs compared `4e81a35` → `50ce799` — commits differing **only** in `__version__` and a date string. The answer was knowable in advance: no change.

| Run | Repeats | Verdict | Truth |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 per side | `REGRESSION` (42% slower) | ❌ |
| 2 | 2 per side | `IMPROVEMENT` (9.6% faster) | ❌ |

Both times the **answer diff was perfect** — 120/120 identical, `max|dp| = 0.000000`. Only the timing rule was broken.

**Why it was broken.** I compared a median difference against `max(range/median, 3%)`. A range isn't a statistical test — it has no notion of how likely a separation is by chance. In run 2 the candidate's two samples happened to land 2.9% apart while the baseline's spanned 9.3%, so the threshold collapsed and a 9.6% drift cleared it by 0.3 points.

I'd told you those were "two independent guards" that couldn't both be fooled. That was wrong twice over: at n=1 the noise floor is 0 by construction, so there was only ever one guard; and a range-based guard is defeated by exactly the luck that defeated it.

def power() -> dict:
    """Power source and whether macOS Low Power Mode is throttling the machine.

    Low Power Mode caps CPU and GPU frequency and is configured per power source, so on this machine it switches on
    automatically on battery. It is invisible to `pmset -g batt` and accounts for most of the battery penalty
    measured here: mini `mps` lat2_ms was 248.7 ms on AC against about 348 ms on battery. A record measured under it
    is not comparable with one measured without it, so it is reported and gated like the power source itself.
    """
    text = _run(["pmset", "-g", "batt"])
    # `pmset -g` prints the settings in force now; `-g custom` prints a block per source, which is the configuration
    # rather than the current state.
    live = _run(["pmset", "-g"])
    match = re.search(r"^\s*lowpowermode\s+(\d+)\s*$", live, re.MULTILINE)
    low_power = None if match is None else match.group(1) == "1"
    return {"source": "AC" if "AC Power" in text else "battery" if text else "unknown",
            "low_power_mode": low_power, "raw": text.splitlines()[:1]}

feat(preflight): detect macOS Low Power Mode, which pmset -g batt does not show

This machine has lowpowermode set to 1 for battery and 0 for AC, so unplugging
silently caps CPU and GPU frequency. It is invisible to `pmset -g batt`, which is
all the harness was reading, and it accounts for most of the battery penalty
measured here: mini mps lat2_ms was 248.7 ms on AC against about 348 ms on
battery, far more than thermal drift alone explains.

The consequence for records is the same as for the power source: one measured
under Low Power Mode is not comparable with one measured without it. So it is
read from `pmset -g` (the settings in force, not `-g custom` which lists the
configuration per source), gated for benchmarking, sampled again at the end, and
printed in record.md as part of the power line. Its absence is recorded
positively, so an old record is not mistaken for an unchecked one.

The mid-run change detection now covers the governor as well as the source,
because on this machine they move together: attaching power switches Low Power
Mode off, which is a step change in throughput halfway through a run even though
the thermal situation improves.
MSG
git push -q origin main && echo pushed

I've found the root cause, and it's a concrete fix rather than a vague "flaky cable."

## Your charger is a 15W phone charger, not a Mac charger

```
Wattage = 15W
Current = 3000mA
Voltage = 5000mV     ← 5V, so USB-PD never negotiated a higher voltage
```

A MacBook Air M4 ships with a **30W or 35W** adapter. Under sustained GPU load this machine draws well above 15W, so supply loses to demand and macOS falls back to battery — which switches Low Power Mode **on**, capping CPU and GPU frequency. When load eases it flips back to AC and Low Power Mode off.

The 60-second sample caught it mid-oscillation:

| Time | Source | Low Power Mode |
|---|---|---|
| 11:32:57 | Battery | **1** |
| 11:33:09 | AC | 0 |
| 11:33:21 | AC | 0 |
| 11:33:28 | Battery | **1** |
| 11:33:52 | Battery | **1** |

Three state changes in under a minute, each one a step change in CPU/GPU ceiling.

This explains every anomaly in one stroke: the "AC attached; not charging" readings (15W can't charge while the system draws more), the ~40% battery penalty (248.7 ms → ~348 ms, Low Power Mode rather than thermals), and why it destabilizes specifically during benchmarks.

**What I need: plug in the 30W/35W Apple adapter directly, not through a hub.** Then `preflight` will pass on its own and I won't need `--skip-preflight-gates`.

## Consequence for the run in flight

The 5-repeat dry run is still going and has crossed power/governor boundaries repeatedly. **Its timing data is unusable** — not noisy, but structurally invalid, since different repeats ran under different frequency ceilings. Worse, it started before I added the detection, so it won't flag this itself.

I'll let it finish for the mechanical validation (does a 5-repeat run complete and write a record), then discard its timing conclusions. The answer-diff portion remains valid — correctness doesn't care about clock speed.

## What went in meanwhile

`preflight` now reads Low Power Mode from `pmset -g` (invisible to `pmset -g batt`, which is all I was checking), gates on it, samples it again at the end, and `record.md` prints it — recording its *absence* positively too, so an old record isn't mistaken for an unchecked one. The mid-run change detector now covers the governor, not just the source. 117 tests passing, pushed.

Had I not checked this, your first real optimization record would have been measured across an oscillating frequency ceiling, and I'd have reported whatever it produced.

def run_bench(rec: Recorder, python: str, tree: Path, unit: Unit, modes: tuple[str, ...], profile: Profile,
              side: Side, rep: int, questions: Path, gguf: Path | None) -> None:
    """All of a unit's modes in one basal-bench run, with a per-mode retry if that run produced nothing.

    basal-bench writes its --out file only after every mode has finished, so one mode failing - the 4.5B model
    quantising at load in `mlx-q8` is the plausible candidate on a 16 GB machine - discards the measurements of
    every mode that worked. In a profile that takes hours, losing a whole unit to one bad mode is expensive, so the
    modes are retried individually to salvage the rest. A per-mode run has no in-run `agree` column, which is a
    lesser loss than the timings: basal-agree measures agreement properly anyway.
    """
    stem = ("bench", unit.label, side.value, f"rep{rep}")
    out = rec.out(*stem)
    argv = phases.bench(python, unit, modes, questions, profile.bench_n, profile.bench_lat_n, out, gguf)
    rec.timed(f"bench {unit.label} {side.value} rep{rep}",
              lambda: run_logged(argv, tree, rec.log(*stem), timeout=PHASE_TIMEOUT_S))
    payload = metrics.read_json(out)
    if payload:
        metrics.absorb_bench(rec.series, unit.label, side, payload)
        return
    if len(modes) < 2:
        return
    for mode in modes:
        per_stem = (*stem, mode)
        per_out = rec.out(*per_stem)
        rec.timed(f"bench {unit.label} {mode} {side.value} rep{rep} (salvage)",
                  lambda m=mode, o=per_out, s=per_stem: run_logged(
                      phases.bench(python, unit, (m,), questions, profile.bench_n, profile.bench_lat_n, o, gguf),
                      tree, rec.log(*s), timeout=PHASE_TIMEOUT_S))
        metrics.absorb_bench(rec.series, unit.label, side, metrics.read_json(per_out))

"""Tests for the mechanism: worktrees must isolate each commit and survive a killed run.

These use a real throwaway git repository, because the behaviour under test is git's.

  cd harness && python -m pytest test_execute.py -q
"""
import subprocess

import pytest

from execute import Result, check_shadowing, free_port, resolve_gguf, resolved_basal, worktree


def git(repo, *args):
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout


@pytest.fixture
def repo(tmp_path):
    """A repository with two commits whose `basal` package reports different versions."""
    root = tmp_path / "repo"
    (root / "basal").mkdir(parents=True)
    git_dir = ["-c", "user.name=t", "-c", "user.email=t@example.com"]
    subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", "-b", "main", str(root)], check=True, capture_output=True)
    for version in ("1.0", "2.0"):
        (root / "basal" / "__init__.py").write_text(f'__version__ = "{version}"\n', encoding="utf-8")
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), *git_dir, "add", "-A"], check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), *git_dir, "commit", "-q", "-m", version],
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
    return root


def test_given_a_commit_when_a_worktree_is_made_then_it_holds_that_commits_code(repo, tmp_path):
    first = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD~1").strip()
    with worktree(repo, first, tmp_path / "wt") as tree:
        assert (tree / "basal" / "__init__.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() == '__version__ = "1.0"'


def test_given_a_worktree_when_the_block_exits_then_it_is_removed(repo, tmp_path):
    head = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
    path = tmp_path / "wt"
    with worktree(repo, head, path):
        assert path.exists()
    assert not path.exists()
    assert str(path) not in git(repo, "worktree", "list")


def test_given_a_worktree_leaked_by_a_killed_run_when_reused_then_it_is_reclaimed(repo, tmp_path):
    """This machine loses power under load, so a killed run is realistic. The next run must not be blocked by it."""
    head = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
    path = tmp_path / "wt"
    # simulate a kill: add the worktree and never release it
    subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(path), head],
                   check=True, capture_output=True)
    assert str(path) in git(repo, "worktree", "list")
    with worktree(repo, head, path) as tree:          # must not raise "already exists"
        assert (tree / "basal" / "__init__.py").exists()


def test_given_a_stale_directory_in_the_way_when_a_worktree_is_made_then_it_is_cleared(repo, tmp_path):
    head = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
    path = tmp_path / "wt"
    path.mkdir()
    (path / "junk.txt").write_text("left over", encoding="utf-8")
    with worktree(repo, head, path) as tree:
        assert not (tree / "junk.txt").exists()


def test_given_two_worktrees_of_different_commits_then_each_imports_its_own_code(repo, tmp_path):
    """The whole harness rests on this: `python -m` puts the worktree first on sys.path."""
    import sys
    first, second = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD~1").strip(), git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
    with worktree(repo, first, tmp_path / "a") as a, worktree(repo, second, tmp_path / "b") as b:
        check_shadowing(sys.executable, a)
        check_shadowing(sys.executable, b)
        assert resolved_basal(sys.executable, a) != resolved_basal(sys.executable, b)
        versions = [subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", "import basal;print(basal.__version__)"], cwd=tree,
                                   capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
                    for tree in (a, b)]
        assert versions == ["1.0", "2.0"]


def test_given_a_directory_without_basal_when_shadowing_checked_then_it_raises(tmp_path):
    """A silent failure here would mean every number in every record described other code."""
    import sys
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        check_shadowing(sys.executable, tmp_path)


def test_given_a_free_port_then_it_can_be_bound():
    import socket
    port = free_port()
    with socket.socket() as s:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))


def test_given_a_unit_with_no_gguf_declared_when_resolved_then_none_rather_than_a_download():
    assert resolve_gguf(None, None) is None
    assert resolve_gguf("Remek/whatever", None) is None
    assert resolve_gguf(None, "file.gguf") is None


def test_given_a_result_then_ok_follows_the_exit_status(tmp_path):
    assert Result(argv=["x"], returncode=0, log=tmp_path / "l").ok
    assert not Result(argv=["x"], returncode=1, log=tmp_path / "l").ok

These use a real throwaway git repository, because the behaviour under test is git's.

def git(repo, *args):
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout


@pytest.fixture
def repo(tmp_path):
    """A repository with two commits whose `basal` package reports different versions."""
    root = tmp_path / "repo"
    (root / "basal").mkdir(parents=True)
    git_dir = ["-c", "user.name=t", "-c", "user.email=t@example.com"]
    subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", "-b", "main", str(root)], check=True, capture_output=True)
    for version in ("1.0", "2.0"):

        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), *git_dir, "add", "-A"], check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), *git_dir, "commit", "-q", "-m", version],
                       check=True, capture_output=True)
    return root


def test_given_a_commit_when_a_worktree_is_made_then_it_holds_that_commits_code(repo, tmp_path):
    first = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD~1").strip()
    with worktree(repo, first, tmp_path / "wt") as tree:
        assert (tree / "basal" / "__init__.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() == '__version__ = "1.0"'


def test_given_a_worktree_when_the_block_exits_then_it_is_removed(repo, tmp_path):

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Every single one of the ten metrics shows the candidate slower: −9.8, −21.8, −16.9, −13.7, −12.0, −8.2, −7.3, −4.5, −33.3, −5.9. The order was `B/C C/B B/C C/B B/C`: with **5 repeats — an odd number — the baseline ran first 3 times and the candidate only 2.** Running first means running on a cooler, less-throttled machine. So I built a systematic advantage for the baseline into the design and then reported it as a regression.

The second bug: I ran **10 significance tests at α=0.05 with no multiplicity correction.** The chance of at least one false positive across 10 independent tests is ~40%. Two came back at p=0.032.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

def holm_adjust(comparisons: list[Comparison], alpha: float = ALPHA) -> list[Comparison]:
    """Holm-Bonferroni within each (unit, mode), over the primary metrics that can decide a verdict.

    A record runs one significance test per metric per mode per unit. At alpha each, the chance that at least one
    shows a difference that is not there grows with the count - about 40% across ten tests, and a dry run of two
    commits differing only in a version string duly produced two "WORSE" verdicts at p = 0.032.

    The family is deliberately one (unit, mode), not the whole record. "Did `mps` get faster?" and "did `mlx` get
    faster?" are separate questions about separate backends, not repeated attempts at one; correcting across every
    mode at once would need so many repeats that the harness could never conclude anything. The consequence is
    stated in the record: a run examining many modes can still show one spurious mode, so a lone marginal result
    should be re-run before it is believed.

    Holm is used rather than plain Bonferroni because it is uniformly more powerful at the same family-wise error:
    the p-values are ranked, the i-th of m is compared against alpha / (m - i), and the first failure retains every
    weaker hypothesis after it.
    """
    families: dict[tuple[str, str], list[int]] = {}
    for i, c in enumerate(comparisons):
        if c.metric in PRIMARY_METRICS and c.p_value is not None and c.verdict is not MetricVerdict.UNKNOWN:
            families.setdefault((c.unit, c.mode), []).append(i)

    adjusted = list(comparisons)
    for members in families.values():
        m = len(members)
        ranked = sorted(members, key=lambda i: comparisons[i].p_value or 1.0)
        still_rejecting = True
        for rank, i in enumerate(ranked):
            c = comparisons[i]
            threshold = alpha / (m - rank)
            passes = still_rejecting and (c.p_value or 1.0) <= threshold
            if not passes:
                still_rejecting = False
            if passes or c.verdict not in (MetricVerdict.BETTER, MetricVerdict.WORSE):
                adjusted[i] = replace(c, holm_threshold=threshold)
            else:
                adjusted[i] = replace(
                    c, verdict=MetricVerdict.SAME, holm_threshold=threshold,
                    why_unknown=f"p {c.p_value:.3f} is above the Holm threshold {threshold:.3f} for the {m} "
                                f"primary metric(s) tested on this mode")
    return adjusted

    speed = speed_verdict(comparisons)

# --- the multiplicity correction -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def mode_series(unit, mode, lat_base, lat_cand, rate_base, rate_cand):
    return {(unit, mode, "lat2_ms"): {"baseline": lat_base, "candidate": lat_cand},
            (unit, mode, "dec_s"): {"baseline": rate_base, "candidate": rate_cand}}


def test_given_two_primary_metrics_on_one_mode_when_adjusted_then_the_stricter_bar_is_alpha_over_two():
    """Holm ranks the p-values and compares the i-th of m against alpha/(m-i)."""
    comparisons = holm_adjust(compare_series(mode_series("u", "mps", SLOW, FAST, LOW_RATE, HIGH_RATE)))
    thresholds = sorted(c.holm_threshold for c in comparisons)
    assert thresholds == [ALPHA / 2, ALPHA]


def test_given_a_marginal_p_value_when_adjusted_then_the_verdict_is_withdrawn():
    """The real failure: at a flat alpha, p=0.032 on one of ten tests was reported WORSE. Holm withdraws it."""
    base = [313.9, 344.5, 320.1, 338.0, 325.0, 330.0]
    cand = [399.5, 523.8, 430.4, 450.0, 410.0, 470.0]
    raw = classify(base, cand, Direction.LOWER_BETTER)
    assert raw["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.WORSE          # significant on its own
    assert ALPHA / 2 < raw["p_value"] <= ALPHA            # but only at the unadjusted level
    adjusted = holm_adjust(compare_series(mode_series("u", "mps", base, cand, LOW_RATE, LOW_RATE)))
    withdrawn = [c for c in adjusted if c.metric == "lat2_ms"][0]
    assert withdrawn.verdict is MetricVerdict.SAME
    assert "Holm threshold" in withdrawn.why_unknown


def test_given_a_decisively_separated_metric_when_adjusted_then_the_verdict_survives():
    """The correction must not make the harness unable to detect a real difference."""
    adjusted = holm_adjust(compare_series(mode_series("u", "mps", SLOW, FAST, LOW_RATE, HIGH_RATE)))
    assert all(c.verdict is MetricVerdict.BETTER for c in adjusted)


def test_given_two_modes_when_adjusted_then_each_is_corrected_separately():
    """Backends are separate questions, so testing mlx must not raise the bar for mps."""
    series_both = {**mode_series("u", "mps", SLOW, FAST, LOW_RATE, HIGH_RATE),
                   **mode_series("u", "mlx", SLOW, FAST, LOW_RATE, HIGH_RATE)}
    adjusted = holm_adjust(compare_series(series_both))
    for mode in ("mps", "mlx"):
        thresholds = sorted(c.holm_threshold for c in adjusted if c.mode == mode)
        assert thresholds == [ALPHA / 2, ALPHA]


def test_given_an_unjudgeable_metric_when_adjusted_then_it_is_not_counted_in_the_family():
    """A metric with too few repeats was never tested, so it must not make the bar stricter for the others."""
    series_one = {("u", "mps", "lat2_ms"): {"baseline": SLOW, "candidate": FAST},
                  ("u", "mps", "dec_s"): {"baseline": [1.0], "candidate": [2.0]}}
    adjusted = holm_adjust(compare_series(series_one))
    tested = [c for c in adjusted if c.metric == "lat2_ms"][0]
    assert tested.holm_threshold == ALPHA          # family of one, not two


def test_given_the_assessment_then_the_correction_is_already_applied():
    """assess owns the correction, because it is the only place that knows how many tests the record ran."""
    base = [313.9, 344.5, 320.1, 338.0, 325.0, 330.0]
    cand = [399.5, 523.8, 430.4, 450.0, 410.0, 470.0]
    comparisons = compare_series(mode_series("u", "mps", base, cand, LOW_RATE, LOW_RATE))
    assert assess(comparisons, PASSING, answers_changed=False).overall is Overall.NO_CHANGE


# --- gates ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- the multiplicity correction -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def mode_series(unit, mode, lat_base, lat_cand, rate_base, rate_cand):
    return {(unit, mode, "lat2_ms"): {"baseline": lat_base, "candidate": lat_cand},
            (unit, mode, "dec_s"): {"baseline": rate_base, "candidate": rate_cand}}


def test_given_two_primary_metrics_on_one_mode_when_adjusted_then_the_stricter_bar_is_alpha_over_two():
    """Holm ranks the p-values and compares the i-th of m against alpha/(m-i)."""
    comparisons = holm_adjust(compare_series(mode_series("u", "mps", SLOW, FAST, LOW_RATE, HIGH_RATE)))
    thresholds = sorted(c.holm_threshold for c in comparisons)
    assert thresholds == [ALPHA / 2, ALPHA]


def test_given_a_marginal_p_value_when_adjusted_then_the_verdict_is_withdrawn():
    """The real failure: at a flat alpha, p=0.032 on one of ten tests was reported WORSE. Holm withdraws it."""
    base = [313.9, 344.5, 320.1, 338.0, 325.0, 330.0]
    cand = [399.5, 523.8, 430.4, 450.0, 410.0, 470.0]
    raw = classify(base, cand, Direction.LOWER_BETTER)
    assert raw["verdict"] is MetricVerdict.WORSE          # significant on its own
    assert ALPHA / 2 < raw["p_value"] <= ALPHA            # but only at the unadjusted level
    adjusted = holm_adjust(compare_series(mode_series("u", "mps", base, cand, LOW_RATE, LOW_RATE)))
    withdrawn = [c for c in adjusted if c.metric == "lat2_ms"][0]
    assert withdrawn.verdict is MetricVerdict.SAME
    assert "Holm threshold" in withdrawn.why_unknown


def test_given_a_decisively_separated_metric_when_adjusted_then_the_verdict_survives():
    """The correction must not make the harness unable to detect a real difference."""
    adjusted = holm_adjust(compare_series(mode_series("u", "mps", SLOW, FAST, LOW_RATE, HIGH_RATE)))
    assert all(c.verdict is MetricVerdict.BETTER for c in adjusted)


def test_given_two_modes_when_adjusted_then_each_is_corrected_separately():
    """Backends are separate questions, so testing mlx must not raise the bar for mps."""
    series_both = {**mode_series("u", "mps", SLOW, FAST, LOW_RATE, HIGH_RATE),
                   **mode_series("u", "mlx", SLOW, FAST, LOW_RATE, HIGH_RATE)}
    adjusted = holm_adjust(compare_series(series_both))
    for mode in ("mps", "mlx"):
        thresholds = sorted(c.holm_threshold for c in adjusted if c.mode == mode)
        assert thresholds == [ALPHA / 2, ALPHA]


def test_given_an_unjudgeable_metric_when_adjusted_then_it_is_not_counted_in_the_family():
    """A metric with too few repeats was never tested, so it must not make the bar stricter for the others."""
    series_one = {("u", "mps", "lat2_ms"): {"baseline": SLOW, "candidate": FAST},
                  ("u", "mps", "dec_s"): {"baseline": [1.0], "candidate": [2.0]}}
    adjusted = holm_adjust(compare_series(series_one))
    tested = [c for c in adjusted if c.metric == "lat2_ms"][0]
    assert tested.holm_threshold == ALPHA          # family of one, not two

    """assess owns the correction, because it is the only place that knows how many tests the record ran."""
    base = [313.9, 344.5, 320.1, 338.0, 325.0, 330.0]
    cand = [399.5, 523.8, 430.4, 450.0, 410.0, 470.0]

This is the module that makes the record a *backend* record. Client-side timing tells you a request got faster; it

Two agents sharing one working tree on a 16 GB machine creates risks neither of us can see alone:

| Risk | Consequence |
|---|---|

| Either runs `git add -A` | Sweeps the other's uncommitted work, which is exactly what I did |
| Either runs `git clean` broadly | Deletes the other's in-progress record output |
| Concurrent `git commit`/`push` | Races and index-lock conflicts |

My own rules from here: explicit file paths only, never `git add -A`, `git clean` scoped to `records/`, and lint/test scoped to my modules.

Author: m <maciekbajor@gmail.com>

    feat(backend): record a backend A/B comparison of two basal commits
    
    Completes the backend harness: the orchestrator's dry run and workload
    validation, the tests for the matrix, the schedule and the write path, and the
    documentation and operational skill.
    
    Why a second harness rather than another profile of run_record.py. Two things
    make them structurally different questions. basal/server.py refuses
    --state-cache-gb and --prefix-cache alongside --deterministic, which the commit
    harness passes on every record because its answer diff needs stable forward
    shapes; so that harness cannot measure the two largest backend levers on this
    machine, by construction rather than oversight. And its question set has
    independent states, so no cache can hit and no cache effect can appear in any
    number it records.
    
    One session is one measurement, and every session starts a fresh server.
    Repeating a workload inside a session was the cheaper design and is wrong: the
    second pass asks the same states against a cache the first pass populated, so
    it measures a warm cache while the first measured a cold one, and pooling them
    as repeats of one quantity hides that.
    
    Two axes come out of one set of measurements: A/B across commits answers "did
    my change help", and headroom across server configurations on one commit
    answers "what is configuration worth before touching engine code". The second
    is the number to read first, since a configuration already worth 10x means the
    engine is not the bottleneck.
    
    Two blocking gates that a commit record does not need. `same work` compares
    usage.input_tokens and usage.branches across sides, because a throughput
    difference between sides asked different work is not an optimisation.
    `cache engaged` requires a reuse-expecting workload to have actually reused
    state, because the most likely failure of a cache benchmark is silent: a
    refused flag or a too-small budget yields a clean record saying the cache
    bought nothing, which reads as a measurement when it is a broken run.

---
name: basal-benchmark
description: Benchmark two basal commits against each other on this Mac and commit a detailed record of the result. Use when asked to measure an optimisation, compare a commit against upstream, check whether a change made the inference engine faster, record or re-run a benchmark, or explain a past record. Covers the A/B harness, the correctness gates, this machine's noise floor, and the operational constraints (sandbox, Metal, AC power, the external weights drive) that silently invalidate a run when ignored.
license: Apache-2.0
---

# Recording a basal A/B benchmark

This repository records what two basal commits actually do on **this** machine: a fanless Apple M4 MacBook Air with
16 GB of unified memory. One record = one baseline commit, one candidate commit, every metric the basal CLIs
produce, and a plain verdict.

The harness runs existing basal CLIs and keeps their output verbatim. It adds exactly one thing basal cannot do by
itself: **a cross-commit answer diff**, because `basal-bench`'s `agree` column compares modes *within one run* and
so can never tell you whether your commit changed what the engine decides.

## Read this before running anything

Five constraints. Each one silently produces a worthless record if ignored; the first two produce a *wrong* one.

1. **Run outside the Bash sandbox.** A sandboxed shell cannot reach Metal: `torch.backends.mps.is_available()` is
   `False` and MLX raises `No Metal device available`. Use `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` for every harness and
   `entire` command. The sandbox also blocks writes to this repository (it is outside the session's working
   directory) and to `/Volumes`.
2. **Never call the console scripts** (`basal-bench`, `basal-serve`, …). Always `python -m basal.<module>` from
   inside a worktree, so the worktree's own `basal/` package shadows the copy in `site-packages`. The venv holds a
   **non-editable** install on purpose: an editable one would register a meta-path finder that wins over
   `sys.path` and would silently benchmark the wrong commit. `harness/execute.py:check_shadowing` enforces this and
   the run aborts if it fails.
3. **AC power.** `preflight` refuses to record on battery. A fanless Air throttles differently on battery and the
   numbers are not comparable with other records.
4. **The external drive must be mounted.** `HF_HOME` is `/Volumes/Vimap H3 t7/ai/cache/huggingface`; the weight set
   is about 25 GB and does not fit the internal disk with headroom.
5. **`eager-fp32` does not exist for the 4.5B model here.** fp32 4.5B needs about 18 GB on a 16 GB machine. Only
   `mini` keeps a true fp32 reference; the 4.5B unit's reference is bf16 `mps`. This is in `config.py`, not a flag
   to override.

## Run a record

```bash
cd ~/repos/current/basal-bench-records
~/basal-env/bin/python harness/run_record.py --candidate <your-commit>
```

`--baseline` defaults to `upstream/main` (the newest commit of the original `rkinas/basal`), which is what "compare
against the original repo" means. `--candidate` defaults to `HEAD` of the fork.

| flag | when to use it |
|---|---|
| `--profile quick` | iterating. mini only, `mps` + `mlx`, 1 repeat, ~20 min. **Produces no speed verdict by design** — it answers "does it still run, and do the served answers still match". |
| `--profile standard` | mini + 4.5B, all modes, 6 repeats. Roughly 2-3 h. |
| `--profile thorough` | **the default, and what a committed record should use.** All four units, all modes, 6 interleaved repeats, 30 timed questions per mode. Budget 4–5 hours and do not use the machine meanwhile. |
| `--no-commit` | write the record but leave it uncommitted, for inspecting the harness itself. |
| `--allow-same-commit` | the calibration run: baseline == candidate, which measures this machine's own noise. |
| `--skip-preflight-gates` | records anyway when a gate fails. The record says so. Do not use it to work around battery power. |

## Steps

1. **Confirm the machine.** `~/basal-env/bin/python harness/preflight.py --basal-repo ~/repos/current/basal
   --benchmarking`. Exit 0 means it may record. Fix what it names rather than passing

## Acceptance criteria

A record is acceptable when all of the following hold:

- [ ] `preflight --benchmarking` exited 0, or the record names the gate that was skipped and why.
- [ ] Both sides are recorded as full SHAs in `meta.json`, and they differ (or `--allow-same-commit` was deliberate).
- [ ] `check_shadowing` passed for both worktrees, so each side measured its own code.
- [ ] Every phase in `meta.json["phases"]` is `ok`, or the record and your report name those that are not.
- [ ] `record.md`, `record.json`, `meta.json`, `answers_diff.json` and `raw/` all exist and the raw files are intact.
- [ ] The answer diff ran for at least one mode, so answer equality is actually evidenced.
- [ ] Every reported speed claim is accompanied by its noise floor and threshold.
- [ ] `INDEX.md` has the new line, newest first, and the record is committed and pushed.

Pushed. Waiting on the calibration run, which is the last gate before any of this is trustworthy.

## Where the deliverables stand

| Deliverable | Status |
|---|---|
| Machine prepared for basal's benchmarks | ✅ verified — 2623 basal tests pass on the baseline |
| Separate Entire repo for records | ✅ `/et/basal-benchmarks/records`, 18 commits |
| Explicit commit recording | ✅ full SHAs, subjects, dates, dependency drift, both sides |
| All available metrics | ✅ bench, order-check, agree, loadtest, determinism, pytest, plus a cross-commit answer diff |
| Clear better/worse/same verdict | ✅ 7 verdicts, correctness gates first |
| Agent skill | ✅ 216 lines, corrected against a day of real running |
| **A validated record** | ⏳ calibration in flight |

## The honest summary of today

The harness is complete and, I now believe, statistically sound. But the thing worth saying plainly is that **it told me I was wrong three times, and each time I was.**

| Attempt | Reported | Actual defect |
|---|---|---|
| 1 repeat | `REGRESSION` 42% | noise floor is 0 at n=1 — my "two independent guards" was one guard |
| 2 repeats | `IMPROVEMENT` 9.6% | a range is not a statistical test |
| 5 repeats | `REGRESSION` | odd count biased the schedule; 10 uncorrected tests at α=0.05 |

All three used commits differing only in a version string, which is the only reason I caught them. Had I validated against a *plausible-looking* optimisation instead, I'd have reported a 42% regression as fact.

The statistics are now an exact rank-sum permutation test with Holm correction, a minimum of 6 even repeats derived from `2/C(2n,n) ≤ α/2` rather than chosen, and all three failure datasets kept as regression tests.

## Two blockers that are yours, not mine

1. **A 30W/35W charger, connected directly.** The 15W supply oscillates the frequency ceiling mid-run. This is the single thing preventing a valid timing record.
2. **Exclusive GPU** when the thorough run happens — the other session's harness and mine cannot both hold models on 16 GB.

When the calibration finishes I'll tell you whether the guards held under the worst conditions. If it reports anything other than "no change", I'll keep digging rather than adjust thresholds until it agrees with me.

Two detectors I added hours earlier fired on their first live run: the power sampler caught a genuine mid-run transition (*started* on battery with Low Power Mode on, *finished* on AC with it off) and the record leads with "the timing comparison in this record is not trustworthy."

## The number that matters for your work

**Under today's conditions this machine cannot detect an optimisation smaller than about 25%.** That's the 15W charger oscillating the governor, not the engine or the harness. Re-run the calibration once a 30W supply is connected — the comparison point is now committed.

## Delivered

- **Machine prepared** — Python 3.12.13 arm64, torch 2.15.0 + MPS, MLX, llama-cpp-python; all six checkpoints (~34 GB); 2623 basal tests green on the baseline
- **`/et/basal-benchmarks/records`** — 19 commits, `basal-copy` deleted
- **Harness** — every basal CLI's output kept verbatim, plus the cross-commit answer diff basal can't do itself; 134 of my tests (200 with the other session's), ruff clean
- **`basal-benchmark` skill** — the operational constraints that silently invalidate a run, written from a day of actually hitting them
- **One validated record**

## What I'd want you to take away

The harness told me I was wrong three times — 42% "regression", 9.6% "improvement", then another "regression" — all on commits differing only in a version string. Each was a real defect of mine: a noise floor that is zero at n=1, a range used as if it were a test, an odd repeat count that biased the schedule, and ten uncorrected tests at α=0.05.

I caught them only because I validated against a pair whose answer I already knew. Had I validated against a plausible-looking optimisation, I would have reported a 42% regression as fact. That's the part of today's work I'd actually trust: not that the harness is right, but that it now refuses to speak when it cannot know.

**Before your first real optimisation record:** a 30W/35W charger connected directly, and the other session's harness idle so only one thing holds the GPU.

What actually ran on your machine:

| Component | Status |

| `basal-bench` on `mps` and `mlx` | ✅ 12 runs, real numbers |
| `basal-serve` + `basal-run` (HTTP) | ✅ 2 servers started, 120 items answered each |

| Worktree isolation | ✅ each commit imported its own code |

| `basal-2.0-4.5B` | ✅ loads and answers, 9.13 GB peak, acc 0.875 |

Four full records were produced today (at 1, 2, 5 and 6 repeats). Nothing is theoretical.

**The distinction that matters:** the benchmark *works*; its **timing numbers aren't trustworthy yet**. Those are two different things and only the second is blocked.

- ✅ **Works and is trustworthy now:** does the engine still run, does it still give the same answers, does accuracy hold, does memory fit. The answer diff is exact and unaffected by clock speed — identical code produced byte-identical probabilities across 120 items.
- ⚠️ **Works but isn't trustworthy yet:** latency and throughput. Comparing a commit *with itself* showed differences up to **−25.3%** purely from the 15W charger oscillating the CPU/GPU frequency ceiling mid-run. The harness correctly reported `NO CHANGE`, but it means a real optimisation under 25% would be invisible today.

**One thing to fix and it's trustworthy for timing too:** a 30W or 35W charger, connected directly rather than through a hub. Then re-run the calibration (`--baseline HEAD --candidate HEAD --allow-same-commit`) and the noise figure should drop sharply — the one stable-AC measurement I got showed mini `mps` at 248.7 ms versus the ~400–470 ms seen while oscillating.

So: you can start optimising and use it today for correctness and for large wins. For measuring anything subtle, it needs the charger.
